What We Do

Full-Service Rheumatology Revenue Cycle Management

Rheumatology billing centers on high-cost biologic drug billing, infusion administration coding, joint and soft tissue injection procedure revenue, and prior authorization management across complex payer networks. PMEX manages every element inside your existing rheumatology practice workflow.

Biologic Infusion Billing

Infliximab, abatacept, and rituximab J-codes billed from infusion nursing records.

Infusion Administration Coding

Initial and sequential infusion codes applied per CMS infusion sequence guidelines.

Joint Injection Billing

Arthrocentesis (20600 to 20611) coded by joint size and with or without imaging guidance.

DMARD Prior Authorization

Methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, and biologic step therapy authorization managed.

Biosimilar Tracking

Correct Q-codes applied when biosimilar substitution occurs at the pharmacy.

Subcutaneous Biologic Coding

Self-administered biologic training (96401) and monitoring codes billed correctly.

Sound Familiar?

Common Rheumatology Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Infliximab J-code quantity billed at vial size, not at the weight-based administered dose.

PMEX verifies the administered dose from the infusion nursing record and bills the correct J-code units per the weight-based calculation.

Biosimilar substituted at pharmacy but branded J-code submitted on the claim.

PMEX tracks biosimilar substitution at the pharmacy level and applies the correct Q-code on every claim where a biosimilar was dispensed.

Joint injection billed without ultrasound guidance add-on when guidance was used.

PMEX bills 76942 (ultrasound guidance) alongside the arthrocentesis code on every injection where guidance is documented.

Biologic step therapy documentation missing when prior auth requires prior DMARD failure.

PMEX compiles step therapy documentation before submitting the biologic authorization request.

Sequential infusion code used when concurrent infusion timing is documented in the nursing record.

PMEX reviews infusion start and stop times from the nursing record before assigning sequential vs. concurrent infusion codes.

Biologic authorization expires mid-cycle, generating retroactive denial on a high-cost drug.

PMEX tracks biologic auth expiration per patient and initiates renewal 14 days before the next infusion date.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Rheumatology Billing

Rheumatology practices lose 18 to 28 percent of revenue to drug quantity errors, biosimilar coding mistakes, and step therapy documentation gaps.

PATTERN 01

Infliximab Dose Billed at Vial Size, Not Administered Quantity

Patient receives 500mg infliximab IV. J1745 is billed per 10mg. Correct units: 50. Billing team submits 10 units (one vial). 80 percent of drug revenue lost on every infusion with this systematic error.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX calculates the J-code billing units from the administered weight-based dose in the infusion nursing record, dividing total milligrams administered by the per-unit descriptor on every biologic infusion claim.

PATTERN 02

Branded J-Code Submitted After Biosimilar Dispensed

Pharmacy substitutes infliximab-dyyb (Inflectra) for branded Remicade. Claim submitted with J1745 (branded infliximab). Correct code: Q5102 (infliximab-dyyb biosimilar). Payer adjudicates at wrong rate or denies for incorrect J-code. Compliance exposure created.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks biosimilar substitution records from the pharmacy and applies the correct Q-code for every biologic infusion claim where a biosimilar was dispensed, updated as FDA approvals expand.

PATTERN 03

Biologic Authorization Denied, Step Therapy Not Documented

Patient started on adalimumab for RA. Commercial payer requires prior DMARD failure (methotrexate, at least 3 months) before approving a biologic. Authorization request submitted without the DMARD trial documentation. Auth denied.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX compiles the required step therapy documentation before submitting the biologic prior authorization request, including DMARD trial dates, dosing, and the clinical rationale for transition to biologic therapy.

Questions

Rheumatology Billing Questions Answered

We verify the total administered dose in milligrams from the infusion nursing record and divide by 10 (the J1745 per-unit descriptor) to calculate the billing units. We never use the vial size as the billing quantity.

Q-codes are HCPCS codes for biosimilar drugs. When a biosimilar is dispensed instead of the branded biologic, the Q-code for that specific biosimilar replaces the J-code for the branded drug. We track dispensed biosimilars and apply the correct Q-code on every claim.

Yes, when the visit includes a separately identifiable evaluation beyond the injection decision. We apply modifier 25 to the E/M and bill the injection procedure separately when documentation supports both services.

We compile the required step therapy documentation before submitting the authorization request, including DMARD trial history, duration, dosing, and the clinical rationale for advancing to biologic therapy.

Yes. Some payers have separate step therapy requirements for biosimilars. We track the payer-specific biosimilar authorization requirements and submit the correct documentation for each drug and payer combination.

Within 30 days, with infusion suite billing workflows and biologic authorization tracking active from day one.
